---
title: "About CDC AtlasPlus data"
---

This article explains what the numbers from CDC AtlasPlus mean and where they
can trip you up. It complements [Getting started](getting-started.html), which
shows how to call the functions, and
[Extrapolation to tracts](extrapolation.html), which shows the tract
estimates. It has no code that downloads data.

AtlasPlus has no published API. CDCAtlas uses the endpoints that the AtlasPlus
web application itself uses, and CDC can change them without notice. What
follows was checked against the application and its documentation in
November 2026. Sources are listed at the end.

## What a row's `data_status` means

Every row from `get_atlas()` has a `data_status`:

| `data_status` | What it means | How CDCAtlas handles it |
|---|---|---|
| "Not Suppressed" | CDC published the count. | Kept as it is. |
| "Data suppressed" | CDC withheld a small count. | `impute_suppressed()` fills it in. |
| "Data not available" | CDC has no data for this row. | Kept by `impute_suppressed()`, with or without a count; a row with no count is left out of the tracts, and dropped with `not_available = "drop"`. |

CDC's technical notes give the suppression rules but don't define these
labels. Their meaning here is inferred from those rules.

A few rows marked "Data not available" do have counts. Connecticut's planning
regions in 2017 are an example: they have counts but no population. Any
published count is kept, whatever its status.

### Suppressed is not zero

A suppressed county has cases that CDC didn't publish. Treating it as zero
undercounts. `impute_suppressed()` estimates it instead, from the state's rate
in the same indicator, year and stratum, times the county's population, kept
between `floor` and `cap`. Filling suppressed counts with zero is available as
`method = "zero"`, as a sensitivity analysis.

The suppression rules differ by disease, according to CDC's technical notes:

- **HIV, county level:** in counties under 500,000 people, when the
  population is under 100 or the count is 1 to 4. In counties of 500,000 or
  more, when the population is under 100. Also when a jurisdiction's
  re-release agreement requires it, and when a suppressed cell could be worked
  out from the others (complementary suppression).
- **STIs:** from 2019 data, under the 2017 CSTE re-release rules: when
  "20% of individuals in a group have the specified disease" (CDC's wording)
  or the population is under 100, plus complementary suppression. Data for
  2000 to 2018 follow the 1996 rules.
- **Tuberculosis:** no suppression at the state level. County cells are
  suppressed where populations have fewer than 5 total cases.
- **Viral hepatitis:** "Data not available" when a condition is not
  reportable or the data are unavailable.

So a suppressed HIV county in a county under 500,000 usually has 1 to 4 cases.
But complementary suppression and re-release agreements can hide larger
counts. That is why `cap = 4` is a default, not a hard limit.

## Provisional data and cautions

For HIV, CDC's technical notes say data are based on cases reported through
December 2025, and "Data through 2024 are considered provisional." Data are
preliminary until a 12-month reporting delay has passed, and should not be
used for formal trend analyses.

The AtlasPlus application also says:

> "Due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, data for 2020 and 2021 may need
> to be interpreted with caution."

> "CDC has postponed release of estimates for HIV incidence, HIV prevalence,
> and PrEP coverage."

## Rates and denominators

The `rate100000` column is not the same kind of rate for every indicator:

| Indicator | `rate100000` |
|---|---|
| HIV | per 100,000 people aged 13 and older |
| Congenital syphilis | per 100,000 live births |
| Knowledge of Status (`disease = "estimate"`) | a percentage |
| Other indicators | per 100,000 people |

AtlasPlus includes HIV surveillance data only for people aged 13 and older,
so HIV counts and populations are for ages 13 and older.

For Knowledge of Status, the columns hold:

- `rate100000`: the percentage who know their status;
- `lowerci_rate` and `upperci_rate`: the bounds of that percentage;
- `cases`: the number who know their status;
- `population`: the estimated number of people with HIV.

There are no confidence intervals for the counts.

For HIV, cases with unknown race or ethnicity are in the totals but not shown
by race, so rows by race may not add up to the state or national total.

## What AtlasPlus offers for each disease

AtlasPlus's set-up data list, for each indicator, the geographies and groups
it offers. `get_atlas()` follows them.

### Geographies

| `geography` | Diseases |
|---|---|
| `"national"`, `"state"` | all |
| `"county"` | all except hepatitis and congenital syphilis |
| `"msa"` | `"hiv"` only |
| `"region"` | `"estimate"` only |

County data for the HIV estimates (`"estimate"`) cover only the Ending the
HIV Epidemic (EHE) counties, for selected years (AtlasPlus Technical Notes,
1.1 and 1.4.1).

For reported data such as HIV diagnoses, CDC's server doesn't return regions.
The AtlasPlus web page asks for each region's states and adds them up in the
browser. CDCAtlas doesn't do that yet (#83): suppressed state counts would
need care, and rates must be recomputed from cases and populations.

### Age groups

| `disease` | Age groups with `stratify_by = "age"` |
|---|---|
| `"hiv"`, `"estimate"` | 13-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-64, 65+ |
| `"chlamydia"`, `"gonorrhea"`, `"adult syphilis"` | 0-14, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-54, 55-64, 65+, Unknown |
| `"tuberculosis"`, `"hepatitis"` | the same, without Unknown |
| `"congenital syphilis"` | none |

Each set covers that disease's ages once. Congenital syphilis can't be
stratified by race, sex or age.

Cases of unknown age (and unknown race) have no Census population. By default
`extrapolate_from_county()` leaves them out and lists them in
`attr(result, "not_allocated")`. With `unknown_age = "redistribute"` (or
`unknown_race = "redistribute"`) they are shared across the county's known
groups in proportion to their counts.

## State totals and county counts

A state's total is usually larger than the sum of its published county
counts. For HIV prevalence in 2022, the gap was 1,804 in North Carolina,
1,888 in Virginia and 1,555 in Georgia.

Suppressed counties explain part of each gap, but not all of it, if each
holds 1 to 4 cases. One explanation is cases whose county of residence is
unknown or not released. CDC's documentation doesn't say so, though, and
other explanations are not ruled out:

- complementary suppression and re-release agreements can hide more than 4
  cases in a county;
- rows marked "Data not available";
- state and county figures may cover different releases.

`no_county_cases()` reports the difference between each state total and the
county counts supplied, after `impute_suppressed()` has filled in suppressed
counties. The difference also includes any county left out of the data you
pass in. `extrapolate_from_county()` leaves the remainder out by default
(`no_county = "report"`). `no_county = "spread"` shares it across the state's
counties; that treats it as cases with no county, which is an assumption.

For the HIV estimates, the counties are EHE counties only, so most of the
remainder is people in the state's other counties. `no_county_cases()` says
so, and `no_county = "spread"` is refused for them.

## CDC's county map

CDC reports every year on its current county map, not on the map of that
year:

- **Connecticut, 2017:** reported by its nine planning regions, which became
  county-equivalents in the 2020s. In 2017 they have counts but no population.
- **Alaska, 2017:** Chugach (02063) and Copper River (02066), created in 2019
  from Valdez-Cordova, have counts. Valdez-Cordova (02261) is listed with no
  population.
- **Alaska, 2022:** Valdez-Cordova (02261) is still listed beside its
  successors, with no population.

The Census tracts don't match these older years. An ACS 5-year release uses
the tract map of its last year, so 2015–2019 is the last release on 2010
tracts:

| ACS 5-year release | Tract map |
|---|---|
| 2015–2019 | 2010 tracts |
| 2016–2020 and later | 2020 tracts |

`extrapolate_from_county()` uses the 5-year ACS ending in the data year, so
2017 uses 2010 tracts and 2022 uses 2020 tracts. Tract estimates from 2017 and
2022 can't be compared tract by tract.

For ACS releases on 2010 tracts (2006–2010 to 2015–2019), a crosswalk assigns
Connecticut's and Valdez-Cordova's 2010 tracts to the current counties (#30).
ACS 2016–2020 and 2017–2021 use 2020 tracts but still code Connecticut by its
old counties; planning regions first appear in 2018–2022. So Connecticut data
for 2020 and 2021 is left out of tract estimates with a warning that says why
(a recode is #121). Rows left out are listed in
`attr(result, "not_allocated")`.

## Census denominators

`extrapolate_from_county()` shares each county's count across its tracts in
proportion to each tract's population in the same stratum, from the ACS.
This assumes every tract in a county has the same rate within a stratum. The
estimates add up to the county counts by construction, so that alone doesn't
show the pattern across tracts is right.

The populations come from these ACS tables:

- **No stratification, sex and age:** B01001 (sex by age).
- **Race:** B03002 (Hispanic or Latino origin by race) by default. Its groups
  match AtlasPlus's, but it has no ages. For HIV, each tract's race
  populations are scaled by the tract's share of residents aged 13 and older.
  `race_table = "B01001"` uses the race-specific sex-by-age tables instead,
  which have ages, but only their White and Hispanic tables match AtlasPlus's
  groups.

The ACS age bands don't start at 13. Each CDC age group counts the share of
each ACS band its ages cover, assuming ages are spread evenly within a band.
So ages 13 and older, and HIV's 13-24 group, count 2/5 of the 10 to 14 band.
That is an assumption, not a Census figure.

Denominators are for ages 13 and older for HIV, and all ages for other
diseases. Congenital syphilis isn't supported, because its rates are per live
birth.

**Puerto Rico by race:** CDC gives Puerto Rico's counts by race without a
population, so a suppressed municipio row by race can't be estimated. Those
rows are left out.

## FIPS codes

The `fips` column is character, zero-padded: two digits for states and five
for counties. Keep it as character when joining to Census data, so leading
zeros aren't lost.

## Saved downloads

Each response from CDC is saved on your computer and reused for 30 days, so
the same data aren't downloaded again. Requests are made one disease and one
year at a time (and for counties, one state at a time), so data already
downloaded, alone or as part of a larger request, are reused.

- `get_atlas(refresh = TRUE)` downloads the request again. For county data it
  also refreshes the matching state totals that the later steps use.
- `clear_atlas_cache()` deletes every saved response.

After 30 days the data are downloaded again, which picks up revisions CDC has
made.
